final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence. The response mainly narrows and reframes the same record: it correctly concedes that aggregate readiness is separate from the disclosure/materiality issue, that generic governance guidance does not override internal policy, and that the named-segment gap is the key unresolved fact. That clarification is useful, but it is reinterpretation, not new proof. The critical compliance predicate remains unmet on the admissible record: policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and the record still contains no admissible evidence of resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance. An open legal ticket is not proof that disclosure was required and omitted, but it is also not proof of compliance closure. That distinction matters: it may defeat a stronger accusation about every downstream failure mode, but it is still insufficient for compliant_with_caveats because caveated compliance would require evidence that the caveat was actually handled through one of the policy-approved paths. Here, the caveat itself is the unresolved compliance predicate.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance for the small-business onboarding gap before launch.

The affected segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, which meets the policy's materiality trigger for a contractual customer segment/named launch use case.
Legal review remains open, so the policy predicate is unresolved rather than closed.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness only; they do not satisfy the separate disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement.
Public NIST-style risk guidance and model-card guidance do not override the specific internal release policy.
